status: frozen before candidate implementation inspection and before lifecycle receiver authoring
scope: Linux process lifecycle infrastructure only; actual supervisor helper code, no receiver/browser/product/npm/network execution

required_controls.setup: Create own mock Node and separately-sessioned mock browser group. Register browser ownership while Node is alive; then let Node exit.
required_controls.expect: Verified browser group closes after Node exit; clean result; all signaled targets are the originally registered own identity.

required_controls.setup: Create target own group plus separately-sessioned own sentinel with a different profile marker.
required_controls.expect: Target closes. Sentinel retains exact PID/start identity and remains alive; no signal is attempted against sentinel or its group.

required_controls.setup: Register an own live group, then supply a deliberately different start identity or inconsistent profile/ownership expectation.
required_controls.expect: Cleanup refuses with failure; no signal syscall is attempted against the mismatched group. Original mock remains alive for harness cleanup.

required_controls.setup: Register an own live group then allow it to terminate naturally and reap it before cleanup.
required_controls.expect: Cleanup succeeds as already exited without unsafe signal attempts. A live different-start identity is refusal, not disappearance.

additional_bounded_controls.setup: Using a disclosed syscall adapter, ask an own pipe-waiting mock to exit after final ownership verification but before actual killpg. Reap it, then call the original syscall so the kernel supplies ESRCH.
additional_bounded_controls.expect: Only ProcessLookupError/ESRCH with confirmed no live recorded group members becomes clean already-exited; any live mismatch remains refusal.

additional_bounded_controls.setup: Own mock group explicitly ignores TERM.
additional_bounded_controls.expect: Cleanup escalates to KILL after its bounded grace period, then confirms no live owned member. No other group is signaled.

safety_and_bounds: Each fixture process is created by this harness with a unique owned marker/profile and tracked PID/start_ticks/UID/PGID/SID.
Every real signal is guarded by current process identity and registry membership; any out-of-registry attempt fails before syscall.
All mock children have finite lifetimes; each control including cleanup is bounded to at most30seconds.
Harness finally-cleanup is limited to its own verified identities; no systemwide Chrome/node cleanup, existing profiles or other worker processes.
No inferred zero-internal-execution claim from previous browser timeout; this receiver qualifies cleanup infrastructure only.
Exact final corrected wrapper bytes and thin-adapter/harness hashes will be frozen before execution.
Raw stdout/stderr/structured result/process exit are retained, including any failures; no silent retry.
interface_boundary: Pending author extraction of identical module-level lifecycle helper/class, used by main; no substitute implementation in receiver.
